reviews.review:
A game so soul-crushingly repetitive it has convinced me that I was born to farm, destined to suffer, and cursed to never actually get the part I need. I don’t play Warframe anymore, Warframe plays me. I log in, blink, and suddenly it’s 3 a.m. and I’ve been killing the same dude for eight hours straight because a robot in space told me I might get one piece of something I’ll never finish.

The grind isn’t a mechanic it’s a religion. I’ve farmed so long I’ve started naming the enemies. I’ve stared at drop tables longer than I’ve stared at actual human faces. RNG is my abusive relationship and I keep crawling back because maybe this time she’ll give me the Neuroptics. Every new update brings new hope, and every new hope brings new pain. I farm for resources I don’t understand to craft weapons I’ll never use for missions I don’t remember starting. My inventory looks like a museum of broken dreams. I tell myself it’s “fun,” but deep down I know it’s Stockholm Syndrome with better graphics. The worst part? I love it. I hate it. I need it. I’ll uninstall, swear I’m done, and within 24 hours I’m back, parkouring through the void like a lab rat chasing a glowing blueprint. Warframe isn’t a game. It’s a job you pay to keep. And I recommend it wholeheartedly, I'd like to say that I said that with freewill, but i cannot.
